lines.text: Do you know how a fire extinguisher works? Fire needs three things. Heat, fuel, and oxygen. Take one away, and it dies.
Inside, everything is under pressure. Squeeze the handle, a valve opens, and the pressure pushes it all out of the nozzle.
Water cools the fire down. Foam lays a blanket over the fuel. Carbon dioxide pushes the oxygen away.
Dry powder goes one step further. It interrupts the chemical reaction that keeps the flames going.
To use one, remember PASS. Pull the pin, aim at the base, squeeze, and sweep from side to side.
So a fire extinguisher just breaks the triangle, as fast as it can.
